body: This error is not specific to version 20.8b1, but happens in 21.7b0 or 21.7b0 (and presumably others) as well. Timing-wise, it seems like this could be related to the release of [setuptools-scm 6.1.1](https://pypi.org/project/setuptools-scm/6.1.1/).
This impacts everyone using black through `pre-commit` (was looking for the issue)
@mbode [21.7b0](https://pypi.org/project/black/21.7b0/#files) has wheel and is installing normally.
@piotrgredowski If I check out the tag, a `pip install .` (as executed by _pre-commit_) fails.
Looks like this is caused by https://github.com/pypa/setuptools_scm/issues/608

> Looks like this is caused by [pypa/setuptools_scm#608](https://github.com/pypa/setuptools_scm/issues/608)

That seems to explain why building form tar.gz does not work - does not explain why wheels were removed.

The wheels weren't removed, they are just failing to install (you see that `20.8b1` is in the list of available versions in the 2nd last line of your error message)
```
ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement black==20.8b1 (from versions: 18.3a0, [ ... ] 20.8b1 [ ... ], 21.7b0)
```
The `pip` error message could be clearer in this case for sure.

Yes, I've seen that list and it was pretty confusing indeed. I just don't understand why on the failing machine it does not mention that it is downloading the `black-20.8b1-py3-none-any.whl` and goes straight to tar.gz. 

Also, if they were not removed why they are not visible here https://pypi.org/project/black/20.8b1/#files?

> 
> 
> Looks like this is caused by [pypa/setuptools_scm#608](https://github.com/pypa/setuptools_scm/issues/608)

Pinning the `setuptools-scm` version in `setup.cfg` might be a good way to avoid these issues in the future.

More explicit instructions for those utilizing `pyproject.toml`. You'll probably want to pin `setuptools_scm` under the `build-system`  field in `pyproject.toml`.

For example, here's a diff for my poetry project
```
 [build-system]
-requires = ["poetry>=0.12"]
+requires = ["poetry>=0.12", "setuptools_scm[toml]==6.1.0" ]
 build-backend = "poetry.masonry.api"
```

The `setuptools-scm` dependency in `setup.cfg` did not have a version specified, leading to the issues described in https://github.com/psf/black/issues/2449 after a faulty release of `setuptools-scm` was published.

Thanks for this report!

Am I correct in thinking that old versions will remain uninstallable, even if we pin setuptools-scm in the future?

> Thanks for this report!
> 
> Am I correct in thinking that old versions will remain uninstallable, even if we pin setuptools-scm in the future?

I'd think so. I still believe that the wheels for some reason disappeared from PyPa as they are not being pulled and the mentioned `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tomli'` only appears when the build from source tar.gz fails.

Older versions should be okay again, as the problematic version of `setuptools_scm` has been [yanked](https://github.com/pypa/setuptools_scm/issues/608#issuecomment-907126215), and a fixed version has been [released](https://github.com/pypa/setuptools_scm/releases/tag/v6.2.0). So all the older versions with the unpinned dependency will now install the newest version which includes the fix.
